observation_summary: The getLInfNorm() method in both ArrayRealVector and OpenMapRealVector returned incorrect values because the implementation used an incorrect accumulation formula (summing instead of finding the maximum).
hypothesis: The implementation of the L-infinity norm calculation was logically flawed. In ArrayRealVector, it used 'max += Math.max(max, Math.abs(a))' instead of 'max = Math.max(max, Math.abs(a))', causing it to accumulate values incorrectly. In OpenMapRealVector, it was summing the values instead of finding the maximum.
prediction: Changing the accumulation operator from '+=' to '=' in ArrayRealVector and replacing the incorrect summation logic in OpenMapRealVector with a proper maximum-finding loop will fix the norm calculation.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows that the core issue was an incorrect computational procedure (using addition where a maximum selection was required). This is a classic algorithmic error where the procedure for calculating a mathematical norm was implemented incorrectly.
reasoning_summary: The bug is an algorithmic error in the implementation of the L-infinity norm. The fix involves correcting the computational logic (replacing incorrect summation with a maximum selection). This fits the 'Algorithm/Method' category as it is a procedural error in the method's logic, not a missing guard (Checking) or a simple initialization error (Assignment/Initialization).
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'the L_infinity norm of a finite dimensional vector is just the max of the absolute value of its entries.'
The bug report shows the buggy code: 'max += Math.max(max, Math.abs(a));'
The fix diff shows: 'max = Math.max(max, Math.abs(a));'
The bug report shows the buggy OpenMapRealVector code: 'max += iter.value();'

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves changing an assignment operator, the root cause is the incorrect computational logic (summing instead of finding the maximum) within the loop, which is an algorithmic flaw.
There is no missing guard or conditional validation; the logic itself is fundamentally incorrect.
